Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106769; File No. SR-TXSE-2026-041]
October 29, 2026.
On October 16, 2026, Texas Stock Exchange LLC (“TXSE” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder (“Rule 19b-4”),
[
2
]
a proposed rule change to amend TXSE Rule 17.111(d) to modify the generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The proposed rule change is described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons and is approving the proposed rule change (the “Proposal”), on an accelerated basis.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange filed a proposal to amend TXSE Rule 17.111(d), which governs the listing and trading of Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The Exchange proposes to adopt generic listing standards that would permit the Exchange to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act without submitting a separate proposed rule change under Section 19(b) of the Act for each product. The proposed rule change would, among other things: (1) establish eligibility criteria for commodities, commodity-based assets, and securities held by a Trust; (2) permit up to 15% of the net asset value of the Trust's holdings to consist of certain digital commodities and securities that do not otherwise satisfy the applicable eligibility criteria; (3) permit actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares; and (4) establish related disclosure, liquidity, trading halt, firewall, surveillance, and other investor protection requirements. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
) at the Exchange's website (
https://txse.com/​rule-filings
), and at the principal office of the Exchange
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in Sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
TXSE Rule 17.111(d) currently governs the listing and trading of Commodity-Based Trust Shares on the Exchange. Under the existing rule, the Exchange is required to submit a separate proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act before listing Commodity-Based Trust Shares.
[
3
]
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 17.111(d) to establish generic listing standards that would permit the Exchange to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that satisfy the requirements of Rule 17.111(d) pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act. Commodity-Based Trust Shares that do not satisfy the applicable generic listing standards could continue to be listed
(
printed page 69288)
pursuant to a separate proposed rule change under Section 19(b) of the Act.
Background
The proposed standards are substantially similar to generic listing standards previously approved by the Commission for Nasdaq, Cboe BZX, and NYSE Arca.
[
4
]
In July 2026, the Commission approved amendments to Nasdaq's generic listing standards that, among other things, permit up to 15% of the net asset value (“NAV”) of a Trust's holdings to consist of certain digital commodities and securities that do not otherwise satisfy the applicable generic eligibility criteria, add a definition of “digital commodity,” and permit actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares, subject to additional safeguards. The Commission subsequently approved substantially similar amendments for NYSE Arca and Cboe BZX and materially identical amendments for Nasdaq Texas.
[
5
]
The Exchange's proposal incorporates both the original generic listing standards and the subsequent amendments into Rule 17.111(d), with changes necessary to conform the Exchange's existing rule structure, definitions, and cross-references.
Proposal
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 17.111(d) to permit the Exchange to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that satisfy the requirements of Rule 17.111(d) pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act. Rule 19b-4(e) provides that the listing and trading of a new derivative securities product by a self-regulatory organization is not deemed a proposed rule change pursuant to Rule 19b-4(c)(1) if the Commission has approved, pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act, the self-regulatory organization's trading rules, procedures, and listing standards for the product class that would include the new derivative securities product and the self-regulatory organization has a surveillance program for the product class.
[
6
]
Consistent with the Commission-approved generic listing standards, the Exchange would retain the ability to submit a proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that do not satisfy one or more of the applicable generic listing standards. The proposed rule would also provide that statements or representations contained in any such proposed rule change concerning (1) the description of the index, Trust holdings, or reference assets; (2) limitations on the index, Trust holdings, or reference assets; (3) the dissemination and availability of the index, Trust holdings, reference assets, or Intraday Indicative Values; or (4) the applicability of Exchange listing rules would constitute continued listing requirements. An issuer would be required to notify the Exchange of any failure to comply with such continued listing requirements. If the Commodity-Based Trust Shares do not satisfy those requirements, the Exchange may suspend trading and will initiate delisting proceedings under the TXSE Rule Series 16.500.
Definitions
The Exchange also proposes to modernize the definition of Commodity-Based Trust Shares in renumbered Rule 17.111(d)(3). As proposed, Commodity-Based Trust Shares could be issued by a trust, limited liability company, partnership, or other similar entity that, if applicable, is operated by a registered commodity pool operator pursuant to the Commodity Exchange Act and is not registered as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, or a series or class thereof. Consistent with its stated investment objective and policies, a Trust could hold one or more commodities or commodity-based assets and, in addition, securities, cash and cash equivalents. The proposed rule would also retain the existing creation and redemption structure, as expanded to accommodate the broader range of permitted holdings and cash creations and redemptions based on the next determined NAV per Trust share.
The Exchange also proposes to amend the definition of “commodity” in Rule 17.111(d)(3)(B) to provide that the term is defined in Section 1a(9) of the Commodity Exchange Act and does not include an “excluded commodity” as defined in Section 1a(19) of the Commodity Exchange Act.
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(C) would define the term “commodity-based asset” as any future, option, or swap on a commodity, as defined in proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(B).
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(D) would define the term “digital commodity” as a commodity that is a digital asset and is intrinsically linked to and derives its value from the programmatic operation of a functional crypto system, as well as supply and demand dynamics, rather than from the expectation of profits from the essential managerial efforts of others.
[
7
]
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(E) would define the term “cash equivalent” as a short-term instrument with a maturity of less than three months consisting of: (1) U.S. Government securities, including bills, notes, and bonds differing as to maturity and rates of interest, that are either issued or guaranteed by the U.S. Treasury or by U.S. Government agencies or instrumentalities; (2) certificates of deposit issued against funds deposited in a bank or savings and loan association; (3) bankers' acceptances; (4) repurchase agreements and reverse repurchase agreements; (5) bank time deposits; (6) commercial paper; and (7) money market funds.
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(F) would define “net asset value” as the value of Commodity-Based Trust Shares used in computing periodically the current price for purposes of creation and redemption of Trust shares and reflecting the current market value of the assets held by the Trust, less expenses and liabilities.
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(G) would define “designated contract market” as a board of trade or exchange that has been designated as a contract market under Section 5 of the Commodity Exchange Act and operates under the regulatory oversight of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission pursuant to Section 5 of the Commodity Exchange Act.
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(H) would define “exchange-traded fund” or “ETF” as an open-end management investment company or unit investment trust, as defined in Section 4(2) of the
(
printed page 69289)
Investment Company Act of 1940, or series or class thereof, the shares of which are listed and traded on a national securities exchange, and that has formed and operates under an exemptive order under the Investment Company Act of 1940 or in reliance on an exemptive rule adopted by the Commission.
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(I) would define “Intraday Indicative Value” as the estimated indicative value of a Trust share based on current information regarding the value of the Trust's underlying assets.
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(J) would define “market price” as either the official closing price of a Trust share or, if it more accurately reflects the market value of a Trust share at the time as of which the Trust calculates current NAV per share, the midpoint between the national best bid and national best offer as of that time.
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(K) would define “premium or discount” as the positive or negative difference between the market price of a Trust share at the time as of which current NAV is calculated and the Trust's current NAV per share, expressed as a percentage of the Trust share's current NAV per share.
Finally, proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(L) would define “Reporting Authority,” with respect to Commodity-Based Trust Shares, as an institution or reporting service designated by the Exchange or the Trust as the official source for calculating and reporting information relating to the Commodity-Based Trust Shares, including, but not limited to, portfolio information, the amount of any cash distribution to holders, NAV, or other information relating to the issuance, redemption, or trading of the Commodity-Based Trust Shares. A Commodity-Based Trust Share may have more than one Reporting Authority, each performing different functions.
Eligibility Criteria
The proposed eligibility criteria in Rule 17.111(d)(4) would establish the criteria that the holdings of Commodity-Based Trust Shares must satisfy initially and, except as otherwise specified, on a continuing basis. For each commodity held by a Trust, or commodity that underlies a commodity-based asset held by a Trust, at least one of three criteria would be required to be satisfied. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(A)(i) provides that the commodity could trade on a market that is a member of the Intermarket Surveillance Group (“ISG”), provided that the Exchange may obtain information about trading in the commodity from the ISG member. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(A)(ii) provides that the commodity could underlie a futures contract that has been made available to trade on a designated contract market for at least six months, provided that the Exchange has a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement, whether directly or through common membership in ISG, with that designated contract market. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(A)(iii) provides that on an initial listing basis only, a commodity would satisfy the eligibility criteria if an exchange-traded fund designed to provide economic exposure of no less than 40% of its NAV to that commodity is listed and traded on a national securities exchange.
The proposed eligibility requirements for the commodity or commodity-based asset components held by the Trust in proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(A)(i) and (ii) are intended to ensure that the Exchange can monitor trading activity in the underlying commodity market or CFTC regulated futures market through a comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement, thereby facilitating the monitoring for fraud and manipulation. The eligibility requirement in proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(A)(iii) is intended to cover underlying commodities that are already substantially investable through existing ETFs, and to prevent regulatory arbitrage between ETPs registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and ETFs registered under the Investment Company Act of 1940.
To the extent a Trust holds securities, proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(B) would require each such security to satisfy the applicable equity or fixed income component requirements of Rule 17.135(b)(1)(A) or (B), or, in the case of a listed option, to trade on an ISG market. Those provisions are the Exchange's existing component-security standards for generically listed Managed Fund Shares. The proposed rule therefore would use existing Exchange standards to determine whether securities held by a Trust qualify for purposes of generic listing.
15% Buffer and Digital Commodity
Notwithstanding the foregoing eligibility criteria, proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(C) would permit up to 15% of the NAV of a Trust's holdings in the aggregate to consist of (i) digital commodities that do not satisfy the commodity eligibility criteria in Rule 17.111(d)(4)(A), and/or (ii) securities that do not satisfy the securities eligibility criteria in Rule 17.111(d)(4)(B). For purposes of calculating the 15% limitation, any derivative held by the Trust would be calculated based on its gross notional value.
The proposed 15% buffer is limited to digital commodities and securities that do not otherwise satisfy the applicable eligibility criteria and would not constitute a general exception for other non-qualifying assets. Accordingly, at least 85% of the NAV of the Trust's holdings would continue to consist of commodities, commodity-based assets, and securities satisfying the applicable eligibility criteria and/or cash and cash equivalents. The Trust would otherwise remain subject to all applicable requirements of Rule 17.111(d).
In connection with the 15% buffer, the Exchange proposes to define “digital commodity” to make clear the types of digital assets that may be included within the buffer. The proposed definition is informed by joint interpretive guidance issued by the Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission in March 2026.
[
8
]
The Exchange represents that to the extent legislation is enacted defining “digital commodity” or a substantially similar term, the Exchange will submit a rule filing to conform the definition in Rule 17.111(d) to the statutory definition. The proposed limitation would effectively exclude other commodities, such as non-fungible assets or non-fungible collectibles, from the 15% buffer, but would not preclude the Exchange from submitting a separate proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares holding other commodities. The Exchange notes that generic listing standards are intended to apply to products that were known and contemplated when the standards were adopted and are not intended to encompass novel products or materially distinct structures that were not considered in adopting the standards.
Actively Managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares
The proposed generic listing standards also would permit both passively and actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares to qualify for generic listing. Current TXSE Rule 17.111(d) does not contain a generic listing framework or an express requirement that Commodity-Based Trust Shares track a specified reference asset or index. Rather, the existing rule contemplates Commodity-Based Trust Shares issued by a Trust that holds a
(
printed page 69290)
specified commodity and requires the Exchange to submit a separate proposed rule change under Section 19(b) of the Act before listing such Shares.
When the Commission initially approved generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares for Nasdaq, Cboe BZX, and NYSE Arca in 2025, those standards required the Shares to be designed to reflect the performance of one or more reference assets or an index of reference assets and therefore contemplated passively managed products. In 2026, the Commission approved amendments to those generic listing standards removing that requirement and instead requiring that the Trust's holdings be consistent with its stated investment objective and policies, thereby permitting both passive and actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares to qualify for generic listing. Consistent with the current Commission-approved standards, proposed Rule 17.111(d)(3)(A) would adopt the latter formulation. The Commission previously has concluded that the mere addition of active management to a portfolio that otherwise would qualify for generic listing does not affect the portfolio's susceptibility to manipulation or the availability of arbitrage between the product and its underlying portfolio.
[
9
]
In connection with permitting actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares, the proposal would adopt additional safeguards designed to ensure that market participants have equal access to information regarding the Trust's portfolio and to protect against the misuse of material non-public information. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(9)(B) would require the Exchange to halt trading if the Exchange becomes aware that the Trust's NAV or the portfolio information required by Rule 17.111(d)(5)(A) is not disseminated to all market participants at the same time. Trading would remain halted until the applicable information is available to all market participants.
Firewalls and Material Non-Public Information
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(10) would establish information-barrier and material non-public information protections. If the value of a Commodity-Based Trust Share is based in whole or in part on an index maintained by a broker-dealer, proposed Rule 17.111(d)(10)(A) would require the broker-dealer to erect and maintain a firewall around personnel responsible for maintaining the index or who have access to information concerning changes and adjustments to the index. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(10)(B) similarly would require any advisory committee, supervisory board, or similar entity that advises an index licensor or administrator or makes decisions regarding index composition, methodology, and related matters to implement and maintain, or be subject to, procedures designed to prevent the use and dissemination of material non-public information regarding the applicable index.
In addition, proposed Rule 17.111(d)(10)(C) would require any person associated with, or acting as an agent of, the Trust, including a Reporting Authority, that has access to non-public information regarding the portfolio or changes to the portfolio to be subject to procedures designed to prevent the use and dissemination of material non-public information. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(10)(D) would impose additional firewall and written-policy requirements where a Trust is affiliated with an entity that has the ability to influence the price or supply of a commodity, or a commodity underlying a commodity-based asset, held by the Trust.
The first two provisions are substantially similar to protections included in the original Commission-approved generic listing standards, while the latter provisions provide additional protection against the potential misuse of material non-public information relating to an actively managed portfolio.
[
10
]
These safeguards are consistent with the additional protections the Commission approved when permitting actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares under the generic standards. The Commission found that the simultaneous portfolio-information requirement helps ensure transparency regarding the underlying portfolio and reduces the potential for any market participant to obtain an unfair informational advantage.
[
11
]
Disclosure and Liquidity Requirements
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(5) would require a Trust to make specified information available prominently on a publicly available website free of charge. Before the opening of regular trading on the Exchange, the Trust would be required to disclose, as applicable, identifying information, quantities and percentage weightings for its commodities, commodity-based assets, securities, cash and cash equivalents. The Trust also would be required to provide information concerning its prior-business-day NAV, market price and premium or discount; historical premiums and discounts; spread information; liquidity risk policies and procedures; NAV methodology; prior-day trading volume; and effective prospectus.
These disclosure requirements are substantially similar to those approved by the Commission as part of the original generic listing standards and are designed to provide investors and market participants with information regarding the Trust and its holdings that is relevant to the pricing and trading of the Commodity-Based Trust Shares.
[
12
]
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(6) would prohibit a generically listed Trust from seeking, directly or indirectly, investment returns corresponding to a specified multiple of, or an inverse or multiple-inverse relationship to, an index, benchmark or reference value over a predetermined period. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(7) also would require a Trust to maintain written liquidity risk policies and procedures if less than 85% of its assets are readily available on a daily basis to meet redemption requests. Such policies and procedures would be required to be reviewed at least annually and to address, among other things, the Trust's investment strategy and asset liquidity under normal and stressed conditions, available cash and funding sources, and assets that are segregated, pledged, encumbered or otherwise restricted. For purposes of this requirement, an asset would be deemed not readily available to meet redemption requests if it is segregated, pledged, hypothecated, encumbered, or otherwise restricted or prevented from being liquidated, sold, transferred, or assigned within one business day. The Commission previously found that substantially similar requirements promote effective liquidity risk management, reduce the risk that a Trust will be unable to meet redemption obligations, and provide investors with relevant information to assess the characteristics and risks of the Commodity-Based Trust Shares.
[
13
]
(
printed page 69291)
Initial and Continued Listing
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(8) would establish initial and continued listing requirements for Commodity-Based Trust Shares. On an initial basis, the Exchange would establish a minimum number of Commodity-Based Trust Shares required to be outstanding at the commencement of trading and each Trust would be required to have a stated investment objective that it follows under normal market conditions. On a continuing basis, the Exchange would maintain surveillance procedures for Commodity-Based Trust Shares listed under the rule and would consider suspension and initiate delisting proceedings upon the occurrence of specified events. Those events include failure to satisfy applicable minimum holder, shares-outstanding or market-value requirements; failures involving dissemination of applicable underlying reference values or the Intraday Indicative Value; failure to calculate or make NAV available as required; failure to provide the website disclosures required by Rule 17.111(d)(5); failure to comply with representations made in a product-specific Section 19(b) filing; or failure to maintain another requirement of Rule 17.111(d).
Trading Halts
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(9) would establish trading halt provisions corresponding to those continued listing requirements. The Exchange could halt trading upon interruptions involving required reference-asset or index information, the Intraday Indicative Value, or required website disclosures and would be required to halt no later than the beginning of the following trading day if an applicable interruption persists. As discussed above, the proposal also would require an immediate halt if the Exchange becomes aware that NAV or the portfolio information required by Rule 17.111(d)(5)(A) is not available to all market participants at the same time. Commodity-Based Trust Shares trading on the Exchange pursuant to unlisted trading privileges would remain subject to Rule 11.020H.
Upon termination of a Trust, the Commodity-Based Trust Shares issued in connection with such Trust would be removed from Exchange listing. A Trust may terminate in accordance with the provisions of the Trust prospectus, which may provide for termination if the value of the Trust falls below a specified amount.
Other Conforming Changes
The Exchange also proposes to amend the applicability provisions of Rule 17.111(d)(2) to remove the existing reference to the Trust Issued Receipts rules and to clarify that Commodity-Based Trust Shares are included within the definition of “security” or “securities” under the Exchange LLC Agreement and TXSE Rules and are subject to the Exchange's existing rules governing the trading of equity securities. This change reflects the broader range of entity structures and holdings permitted under the proposed generic listing standards.
Finally, the Exchange proposes several conforming amendments necessary to implement the generic listing framework. The Exchange proposes to eliminate existing Rule 17.111(d)(5), which contemplates the designation of an individual underlying commodity for each series of Commodity-Based Trust Shares, and to eliminate the existing provisions concerning the stated term of a Trust, qualifications and changes of trustee, and voting rights. Those provisions reflect the narrower structure contemplated by the existing rule and are no longer necessary in light of the broader range of entities and holdings permitted under the proposed generic standards.
The Exchange proposes to modernize the Market Maker account provisions to apply to accounts involving underlying commodities, commodity-based assets and applicable derivatives and to retain the Exchange's books-and-records authority with respect to such activity. The proposal would retain the existing limitation-of-liability provision, with conforming renumbering, and would revise the Supplementary Material to remove the statement that a Commodity-Based Trust Share is a Trust Issued Receipt holding a specified commodity, renumber the existing prospectus and trading-hours provisions, and add an express requirement that an issuer promptly notify the Exchange of a failure to comply with the continued listing requirements.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
14
]
in general, and specifically with the objectives of Section 6(b)(5),
[
15
]
in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. The Exchange also believes the proposal is consistent with the requirement of Section 6(b)(5) that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes that the proposed amendments to Rule 17.111(d) are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices because the proposed rule establishes specific initial and continued listing standards, asset eligibility criteria, disclosure requirements, surveillance-related requirements, trading halt provisions, liquidity standards, and information-barrier protections applicable to Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The proposed generic listing framework is substantially similar to standards previously approved by the Commission for other national securities exchanges.
[
16
]
Commodity-Based Trust Shares that do not satisfy the applicable generic listing requirements would not be eligible to rely on Rule 19b-4(e), and the Exchange would retain the ability to submit a proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act to seek approval to list and trade such securities.
The Exchange believes that the eligibility criteria in proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4) are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices and to protect investors and the public interest. In particular, the criteria applicable to commodities and commodities underlying commodity-based assets are designed to ensure that the Exchange can obtain information regarding trading in such commodities, either through membership in the Intermarket Surveillance Group or an applicable comprehensive surveillance sharing agreement, or, on an initial listing basis, where the commodity is already substantially investable through an exchange-traded fund meeting the requirements of the proposed rule. These criteria would assist the Exchange in monitoring trading in Commodity-Based Trust Shares and in detecting and deterring violations of Exchange rules and applicable federal securities laws. With respect to securities held by a Trust, proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(B)
(
printed page 69292)
would incorporate the Exchange's existing generic component-security standards applicable to Managed Fund Shares and would require listed options to trade on an ISG market. The Commission previously has found substantially similar requirements applicable to component equity and fixed-income securities to be consistent with the Act.
[
17
]
The Exchange will maintain surveillance procedures for Commodity-Based Trust Shares listed pursuant to proposed Rule 17.111(d), consistent with the requirements of Rule 19b-4(e) under the Act. In addition, the eligibility criteria in proposed Rule 17.111(d)(4)(A)(i) and (ii) are designed to ensure that the Exchange can obtain information regarding trading in applicable underlying commodities or commodity futures through the Intermarket Surveillance Group or comprehensive surveillance-sharing agreements, as applicable. The Exchange believes that these surveillance arrangements, together with its surveillance procedures for trading in Commodity-Based Trust Shares, would assist in detecting and deterring fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices.
As discussed above, the Exchange also believes that the proposed 15% buffer in Rule 17.111(d)(4)(C) is consistent with the Act. Under the proposal, at least 85% of the NAV of a Trust's holdings would continue to consist of commodities, commodity-based assets, and securities satisfying the applicable eligibility criteria and/or cash and cash equivalents. The remaining portion would be limited to digital commodities that do not satisfy the applicable commodity eligibility criteria and/or securities that do not satisfy the applicable securities eligibility criteria. By requiring that the primary exposure of Commodity-Based Trust Shares remain in assets that satisfy established eligibility criteria, the Exchange believes that the proposal would provide flexibility for product innovation while maintaining appropriate investor protections and surveillance capabilities.
The Commission previously has approved comparable structures under which at least 85% of an exchange-traded product's investments consisted of assets that did not raise the same fraud and manipulation concerns and concluded that such a threshold would enable adequate surveillance of the shares by the listing exchange.
[
18
]
The Commission subsequently approved substantially identical 15% buffers as part of the generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares of Nasdaq, NYSE Arca, Cboe BZX, and Nasdaq Texas.
[
19
]
The Exchange therefore believes that the proposed 15% limitation appropriately balances flexibility in portfolio construction with the surveillance and investor-protection objectives underlying the generic listing standards.
The Exchange further believes that defining “digital commodity” and limiting the non-qualifying commodity portion of the 15% buffer to assets satisfying that definition is consistent with the Act because it clearly delineates the types of digital assets that may be included in the buffer while preserving the ability of the Exchange to submit an individual proposed rule change under Section 19(b) of the Act for novel products or materially distinct structures that fall outside the generic standards. This approach provides specificity regarding the assets eligible for generic treatment while preserving an appropriate regulatory process for products not contemplated by the standards.
The Exchange also believes that permitting actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares to qualify for generic listing is consistent with the Act. The Commission previously has approved actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares and concluded that the mere addition of active management to a portfolio that otherwise would satisfy applicable generic listing criteria does not affect the portfolio's susceptibility to manipulation or the availability of arbitrage between the product and its underlying portfolio.
[
20
]
The Commission further has stated that this principle applies to Commodity-Based Trust Shares and that consistent application of listing standards across products providing economic exposure to the same underlying commodities may promote competition and provide investors with additional investment alternatives.
[
21
]
In connection with permitting actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares, the proposal would adopt safeguards regarding the availability of portfolio information and the protection of material non-public information. Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(9)(B) would require the Exchange to halt trading if the Exchange becomes aware that NAV or the portfolio information required by Rule 17.111(d)(5)(A) is not available to all market participants at the same time. This requirement is designed to ensure that market participants have equal access to information concerning the Trust's underlying portfolio that is important to pricing the Commodity-Based Trust Shares and to reduce the potential for any market participant to obtain an unfair informational advantage.
Proposed Rule 17.111(d)(10) also would impose information-barrier and material non-public information protections. The Exchange believes these requirements are designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices and protect investors by establishing barriers against the use or dissemination of material non-public information that could be used to manipulate a series of Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The additional protections applicable to persons with access to non-public portfolio information are substantially similar to protections applicable to other actively managed exchange-traded products and to protections previously approved by the Commission for actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares.
[
22
]
The Exchange further believes that the proposed disclosure, liquidity, initial and continued listing, and trading halt requirements are consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The website disclosure requirements are designed to provide market participants with information concerning a Trust's holdings, NAV, market price, premiums and discounts, liquidity policies, and other information relevant to the pricing and trading of Commodity-Based Trust Shares. The liquidity risk requirements are designed to address circumstances in which a Trust may not have sufficient assets
(
printed page 69293)
readily available to meet redemption requests without significant dilution of remaining shareholders' interests. The initial and continued listing standards, together with the Exchange's surveillance procedures and authority to suspend trading and commence delisting proceedings when applicable requirements are not maintained, are designed to ensure that Commodity-Based Trust Shares remain subject to appropriate standards after commencement of trading. The Commission previously has found substantially similar requirements to be consistent with the Act.
[
23
]
The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change is designed to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market by facilitating the listing and trading of Commodity-Based Trust Shares pursuant to generic listing standards that are substantially similar to standards previously approved by the Commission. The proposal would streamline the current process by eliminating the need for a separate proposed rule change for each qualifying series of Commodity-Based Trust Shares, thereby reducing the time and costs associated with bringing qualifying products to market and providing greater regulatory certainty to issuers, while preserving the applicable listing, disclosure, surveillance, liquidity, trading halt, and information-protection requirements described above.
For the foregoing reasons, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposal would establish generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares substantially similar to those already approved by the Commission for other national securities exchanges, thereby allowing the Exchange to list and trade qualifying products pursuant to Rule 19b-4(e) without submitting a separate proposed rule change for each product. This would reduce the time and costs associated with bringing qualifying products to market and enhance competition among issuers and listing venues.
The proposal would also expand the types of Commodity-Based Trust Shares eligible for generic listing, including actively managed products and products that hold, within the proposed 15% limitation, certain digital commodities or securities that do not otherwise satisfy the applicable eligibility criteria. Such products would remain subject to the Exchange's applicable initial and continued listing, disclosure, surveillance, and other investor-protection requirements. Products that do not satisfy the generic listing standards could continue to be considered pursuant to a separate proposed rule change under Section 19(b) of the Act. Accordingly, the Exchange believes that the proposal would promote competition without imposing an unnecessary burden on intramarket or intermarket competition.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange has neither solicited nor received written comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-TXSE-2026-041 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-041. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-TXSE-2026-041 and should be submitted on or before November 24, 2026.
IV. Commission's Findings and Order Granting Accelerated Approval of Proposed Rule Change
After careful review, the Commission finds that the Proposal is consistent with the Act and rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a national securities exchange.
[
24
]
In particular, the Commission finds that the Proposal is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
25
]
which requires, among other things, that the Exchange's rules be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest and are not designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Proposal conforms the Exchange's rules to the changes the Commission previously considered and approved for generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares.
[
26
]
Rule 19b-4(e) provides that the listing and trading of a new derivative securities product by a national securities exchange shall not be deemed a proposed rule change pursuant to paragraph (c)(1) of Rule 19b-4
[
27
]
if the Commission has approved, pursuant to Section 19(b) of the Act,
[
28
]
the exchange's trading rules, procedures, and listing standards for the product class that would include the new derivatives securities product, and the exchange has a surveillance program for the product class.
[
29
]
The Exchange proposes to adopt a generic listing standards for Commodity-Based Trust Shares to establish eligibility criteria for commodities, commodity-based assets, and securities held by a Trust and establish related disclosure, liquidity, trading halt, firewall, surveillance, and other investor protection requirements that the Commission has previously
(
printed page 69294)
considered and approved in separate Rule 19b-4 filings.
Accordingly, the Proposal fulfills the intended objective of Rule 19b-4(e) by permitting Commodity-Based Trust Shares that satisfy the requirements previously found to be consistent with the Act to commence trading without public comment and Commission approval.
[
30
]
The Exchange's ability to rely on Rule 19b-4(e) to list and trade additional Commodity-Based Trust Shares that meet the applicable requirements and minimum standards will reduce the time frame for bringing the shares to market and thereby reduce the burdens on issuers and other market participants, while also promoting competition.
[
31
]
Finally, Commodity-Based Trust Shares listed pursuant to the Proposal would be required to comply with all applicable requirements of TXSE Rule 17.111(d) and be subject to the rules and procedures of the Exchange that currently govern the trading of equity securities on the Exchange.
[
32
]
The Exchange would continue to be required to submit a rule filing with the Commission when seeking to list and trade Commodity-Based Trust Shares that do not meet the generic listing standards under TXSE Rule 17.111(d).
For the same reasons discussed above, the Commission finds good cause, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act,
[
33
]
for approving the proposed rule change prior to the thirtieth day after the date of publication of the notice of the filing thereof in the
Federal Register
. Accordingly, the Commission finds good cause, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act,
[
34
]
to approve the Proposal on an accelerated basis.
V. Conclusion
This approval order is based on all of the Exchange's representations and descriptions in the Proposal, which the Commission has evaluated as discussed above. For the reasons set forth above, the Commission finds, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act,
[
35
]
that the Proposal is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a national securities exchange, and in particular, with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act.
[
36
]
It is therefore ordered, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act,
[
37
]
that the proposed rule change (SR-TXSE-2026-041) be, and hereby is, approved on an accelerated basis.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
38
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106764; File No. SR-NasdaqTX-2026-050]
October 29, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 22, 2026, Nasdaq Texas, LLC (“Nasdaq Texas” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III, below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend Equity 4, Rule 4120, to align it with that of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC.
The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​nasdaqtx/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
When in September of this year the Exchange updated its rulebook at Equity 1 and Equity 4 to more closely align those rules with the equivalent rules of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq”),
[
3
]
in anticipation of the Exchange becoming a primary listing venue in 2027, the Exchange mistakenly copied an obsolete version of Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120.
The Commission had approved the current version of Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120, back in 2022.
[
4
]
However, this version of the rule did not become operative until August of this year.
[
5
]
This delay in making the 2022 changes operative on Nasdaq led to the Exchange mistakenly copying in its September 2026 filing an obsolete version of Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120. The Exchange proposes to correct this mistake in this filing.
The Exchange proposes to replace in its entirety its current version of Equity 4, Rule 4120, with the version of that rule that is currently found in the Nasdaq rulebook. Therefore, the new
(
printed page 69295)
version of Nasdaq Texas Equity 4, Rule 4120, would be structured as follows:
1. Section (a) (Definitions) defines certain terms that are used in the rule.
2. Section (b) (Regulatory Halts) establishes the Exchange's authority to initiate regulatory halts or pauses in various circumstances, including: halts provided for by the applicable SIP Plan; discretionary Regulatory Halts relating to issuer information, material news, initial public offerings, index warrants, derivative securities products, foreign securities, market disruptions, and Initial ETP Opens; and mandatory Regulatory Halts relating to dissemination issues for derivative securities products, the Limit Up-Limit Down Mechanism, market-wide circuit breakers, Equity Investment Tracking Stocks and Subscription Receipts, and reverse stock splits.
[
6
]
3. Section (c) (Operational Halts) establishes the Exchange's authority and procedures for initiating and terminating Operational Halts, including: the circumstances in which Nasdaq Texas may declare an Operational Halt, notification to the SIP when Nasdaq Texas has concerns about collecting and transmitting quotation or transaction information or has declared an Operational Halt or suspension, and the procedures for resuming trading when Nasdaq Texas determines that trading may resume in a fair and orderly manner.
The changes that the Exchange would make to the Nasdaq rule to tailor it to the Exchange would be the following:
1. Modify references to the operating hours and trading sessions of the Exchange, so that they correctly reflect those of Nasdaq Texas. This includes not carrying over language in Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120, that pertains to Nasdaq's upcoming transition to trading 23 hours a day, 5 days a week.
2. Eliminate references to a direct listing with capital raise, as that option is not present in the Nasdaq Texas rulebook.
3. Update references to “Nasdaq” with “Nasdaq Texas.”
Additionally, the Exchange will not copy references to the CORE FIX order entry protocol that are currently present in Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120. This is because the Exchange, Nasdaq, and Nasdaq PHLX LLC will be imminently submitting separate filings to abandon their plans to deploy the CORE FIX order entry protocol, due to a lack of interest by exchange participants. Therefore, it makes no sense for the Exchange to copy references to CORE FIX in Nasdaq Equity 4, Rule 4120, that will soon become obsolete.
[
7
]
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
8
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
9
]
in particular, in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general to protect investors and the public interest.
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change will remove impediments to, and perfect the mechanism of, a free and open market and a national market system by aligning the Exchange's rulebook at Equity 4, Rule 4120, with the substantially similar rule of Nasdaq, which was previously approved by the Commission, finding it to be consistent with the Act.
The proposal is also consistent with Section 6(b)(5) because it is designed to promote clarity, consistency, and transparency for Participants, issuers, and market participants by replacing stale rule text with the version of Equity 4, Rule 4120, that reflects the Commission-approved Nasdaq framework and the intervening updates already incorporated into Nasdaq's current operative rule. The Commission previously approved Nasdaq's Rule 4120 framework to add categories of regulatory and operational halts, reorganize Rule 4120, incorporate provisions of the applicable equity data plans, and make conforming changes to related rules. In approving that framework, the Commission recognized that the revisions promote a clear and uniform approach to trading halts, improve coordination and certainty among plan participants and market participants, enhance the resiliency and integrity of market systems, and promote fair and orderly markets and investor protection. Nasdaq Texas's proposal advances those same objectives because it would adopt a substantially similar halt framework while tailoring only the exchange name, trading session terminology, and other conforming elements needed to reflect the Exchange's existing rules and operations. The Exchange therefore believes the proposal will reduce confusion, support consistent cross-market halt and resumption procedures, and help Participants understand when the Exchange may halt, pause, or resume trading and how related rules will operate.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change will align the Exchange's rulebook at Equity 4, Rule 4120, with the substantially similar rule of Nasdaq. The proposed rule will apply equally to all Participants of the Exchange. The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose an undue burden on intermarket competition because it is designed to align Nasdaq Texas's rule text with the substantially similar Nasdaq rule and to support harmonized halt and resumption procedures across markets. The proposal also will not impose an undue burden on intramarket competition because it is generally conforming, organizational, or cross-referential in nature and will apply equally to all Participants and market participants subject to the affected rules. The Exchange is not proposing to change the competitive operation of its market or to treat any category of Participant differently; rather, the proposal will make the Exchange's rulebook easier to understand and will reduce the potential for confusion by adopting a framework that the Commission has previously approved for Nasdaq and by tailoring it only as necessary to Nasdaq Texas's naming conventions, trading sessions, and rulebook structure.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
(
printed page 69296)
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
10
]
and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4 thereunder.
[
11
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NasdaqTX-2026-050 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NasdaqTX-2026-050. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NasdaqTX-2026-050 and should be submitted on or before November 24, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
12
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

[Release No. 34-106770; File No. SR-NYSE-2026-52]
October 29, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 19, 2026, New York Stock Exchange LLC (“NYSE” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 2(c) to restore language inadvertently omitted from the recently adopted definition of “associated person.” The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 2 (“Member,” “Membership,” “Member Firm,” etc.) to restore language inadvertently omitted from the proposed definition of “associated person” in a recent rule filing.
[
5
]
More specifically, the proposed change is a technical amendment that would ensure that the persons encompassed by the “approved person” category that the Exchange recently filed to delete are captured by the definition of “associated person” in Rule 2(c) for jurisdictional and all other applicable Exchange rules. The proposed rule change is not intended to effect any substantive change to the scope of the Exchange's jurisdiction.
Background and Proposed Rule Change
On September 18, 2026, the Exchange filed an immediately effective rule change to (1) eliminate the “approved person” registration category as no longer necessary, (2) adopt a new definition of “associated person” in Rule 2(c) based on the definition of associated person in Rule 1011(b) of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, Inc. (“FINRA”) and elements of the current definition of approved person, and (3) make related technical and conforming changes.
[
6
]
The Approved Person Filing is scheduled to become operative on October 18, 2026.
[
7
]
As described in the Approved Person Filing, the Exchange did not intend to expand or narrow the scope of its jurisdiction. Rather, the proposal was designed to ensure that all persons currently encompassed by the approved person category would continue to be covered under the proposed definition of “associated person.” Specifically, the filing stated that proposed Rule 2(c)(3) would include the existing categories of approved persons: (i) persons that control a member organization; (ii) persons engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization; and
(
printed page 69286)
(iii) U.S. registered broker-dealers under common control with a member organization. The filing further explained that the proposed definition of “Control Person” was intended to encompass those same categories.
[
8
]
The Exchange has since determined that the text of proposed Rule 2(c)(3), as filed, inadvertently omitted the clause covering persons engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization. That clause appears in the Exchange's current approved person definition and was intended to be carried forward without substantive change. Consequently, the text of proposed Rule 2(c)(3) is inconsistent with both the description of the proposal and the Exchange's stated intent in the Approved Person Filing, which was to preserve, rather than modify, the existing scope of Exchange jurisdiction. This proposed rule change corrects that inadvertent omission and conforms the rule text to the proposal as described in the Approved Person Filing.
The Exchange accordingly proposes to amend Rule 2(c)(3) to add the phrase “a person engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization,” immediately after “controlled by a member organization,”. As amended, Rule 2(c)(3) would provide that an associated person includes:
(3) any person (excluding a governmental entity) directly or indirectly controlling or controlled by a member organization,
a person engaged in a securities or kindred business that is controlled by a member or member organization,
or a U.S. registered broker-dealer under common control with a member organization (a “Control Person”).
No other changes are proposed to Rule 2.
The Exchange proposes that this proposed rule change become operative on the same date as the Approved Person Filing, and therefore requests that the Commission waive the 30-day operative delay so that this proposed rule change may become operative concurrently with the Approved Person Filing and ensure that the rule text accurately reflects the proposal as originally described before the Approved Person Filing takes effect.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
9
]
in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
In particular, the Exchange believes that the proposed technical correction would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system by ensuring that the text of Rule 2(c) accurately reflects the categories of persons described in the Approved Person Filing, which are the categories the Exchange has treated as within its jurisdiction under the current approved person definition. Restoring the omitted clause would eliminate potential ambiguity as to whether persons engaged in a securities or kindred business controlled by a member or member organization are Control Persons and associated persons under Exchange rules. The Exchange believes this clarity would preserve its ability to exercise jurisdiction over those persons and would thereby protect investors and the public interest.
The Exchange further believes that the proposed change is consistent with the Act because it does not alter the approach described in the Approved Person Filing of defining associated person by reference to FINRA Rule 1011(b) and the definition of associated person of a broker or dealer in Section 3(a)(18) of the Act. The proposed change would simply conform the rule text to the scope of the proposal as described in that filing.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
In accordance with Section 6(b)(8) of the Act,
[
10
]
the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change would not impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change is not intended to address competitive issues but is rather concerned with restoring language so that Rule 2(c) conforms to the Approved Person Filing, and it would apply to all member organizations in the same manner.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
11
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
12
]
thereunder, the Exchange has designated this proposal as one that effects a change that: (i) does not significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) does not impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) by its terms, does not become operative for 30 days after the date of the filing, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest.
[
13
]
A proposed rule change filed pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6) under the Act normally does not become operative for 30 days after the date of its filing. However, Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii)
[
14
]
permits the Commission to designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange requested that the Commission waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposal can become effective upon filing. The Exchange states that the proposal does not significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest because it is a technical correction that conforms the text of Rule 2(c) to the Approved Person Filing and does not change the persons described in that filing or the scope of the Exchange's jurisdiction. The Exchange further states that it does not believe the proposed rule change will impose a significant burden on competition because it would apply to all member organizations in the same manner. Further, the Exchange states that it believes waiver of the operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest because it would put the corrected text of Rule 2(c) in place when the new definition takes effect, which would
(
printed page 69287)
avoid a period in which the rule text does not match the persons described in the Approved Person Filing, and therefore would reduce the potential for investor confusion. For these reasons, and because the proposal does not raise any novel legal or regulatory issues, the Commission finds that waiver of the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Accordingly, the Commission hereby waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change operative upon filing.
[
15
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSE-2026-52 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSE-2026-52. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSE-2026-52 and should be submitted on or before November 24, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
16
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1)
[

[
3
]
notice is hereby given that, on October 21, 2026, NYSE Arca, Inc. (“NYSE Arca” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to change the manner in which the shares of the Bitwise 10 Crypto Index ETF (the “Fund”) are listed and traded on the Exchange. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to change the manner in which the shares of the Fund (“Shares”) are listed and traded on the Exchange. The Shares were originally approved to list and trade on the Exchange pursuant to Rule 8.500-E. The Exchange now proposes to list and trade Shares of the Fund on the Exchange pursuant to Rule 8.201-E (Generic).
The Commission approved the listing and trading of shares of the Fund (the “Shares”) on the Exchange under Rule 8.500-E on July 22, 2025.
[
4
]
Rule 8.500-E governs the listing and trading of Trust Units, which are securities issued by a trust, limited liability company, or other similar entity that, if applicable, is constituted as a commodity pool and that holds investments comprising or otherwise based on any combination of futures contracts, options on futures contracts, forward contracts, swap contracts, commodities, and/or securities.
On July 28, 2026, the Commission approved a proposed rule change to amend Rule 8.201-E (Generic).
[
5
]
Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, allows for up to 15% of a trust's net asset value (NAV) to consist of digital commodities or securities that do not independently meet the core generic eligibility criteria; adds “digital commodity”
[
6
]
as a defined term; and allows for actively managed Commodity-Based Trust Shares.
[
7
]
The Exchange proposes to now list and trade the Shares of the Fund pursuant to the generic listing standards set forth in Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, which would permit the Fund to operate in reliance on the generic listing standards in Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, instead of the terms of the Original Approval Order. The Exchange represents that the Shares will meet the requirements of Rule 8.201-E (Generic), as amended, on an initial and continued listing basis. In addition, the Exchange will comply with the requirements of Rule 19b-4(e) to list and trade Shares of the Fund on the Exchange.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b)
[
8
]
of the Act. Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
9
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to
(
printed page 69284)
and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.

AGENCY:
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), DOT.
ACTION:
Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
SUMMARY:
The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 90-19-02, which applies to all MD Helicopters, LLC (type certificate previously held by McDonnell Douglas Helicopter Company) Model 369, 369A, 369D, 369E, 369F, 369FF, 369H, 369HE, 369HM, and 369HS, helicopters, that are equipped with a cargo hook. AD 90-19-02 requires replacing the overrunning clutch assembly and sprag assembly with airworthy parts and repetitively inspecting the sprag assembly, clutch inner and outer races of the overrunning clutch assembly. Since the FAA issued AD 90-19-02, after further analysis the FAA determined that additional helicopter models are affected by this unsafe condition. This proposed AD would expand the applicability and would require removing certain overrunning clutch assemblies and certain overrunning clutch subassemblies from service, installing or replacing parts, and reidentifying certain overrunning clutch assemblies, as applicable. This proposed AD would also require for certain model helicopters, revising the Airworthiness Limitations Section (ALS) of the existing aircraft maintenance manual (AMM) or instructions for continued airworthiness (ICA) and the existing approved maintenance or inspection program, as applicable. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.
DATES:
The FAA must receive comments on this proposed AD by December 18, 2026.

Comments Invited
The FAA invites you to send any written relevant data, views, or arguments about this proposal. Send your comments using a method listed under
ADDRESSES
